newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil opens tap on Sleipner West gas field.
newsitem.headline: Statoil opens tap on Sleipner West gas field.

text.p: Norwegian state oil company Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap ASA said on Wednesday gas had started to flow from the Sleipner West development in the North Sea one month ahead of schedule.
Condensate from the field was expected to begin in the next 24 hours, the company said.

Gas from the development will form part of the deliveries under the Troll agreements, and will flow to continental Europe via the Zeepipe line to Zeebrugge in Belgium. Deliveries from the field will begin in September.
Condensate and natural gas liquids (NGLs) will be piped for processing to the terminal at Kaarstoe, north of Stavanger on Norway's west coast.
Recoverable reserves at the field are estimated at 127 billion cubic metres of gas and 325 million barrels of condensate and NGLs.
The Sleipner West development comprises two platforms, the unmanned Sleipner B wellhead unit and the T gas treatment installation.

The T-platform will reduce the level of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the gas to around 2.5 percent from nine percent, as required under sales specifications. About one million tonnes per year of CO2 will be removed and disposed of by injecting it about 1,000 metres below the seabed.
Statoil said it was the first time CO2 had been compressed and injected underground on an offshore platform.
Partners in Sleipner West are Statoil with 49.50 percent, Exxon Corp's Esso with 32.24 percent, Norsk Hydro ASA with 8.85 percent, Elf Aquitaine with 8.47 percent and Total SA with 0.94 percent.
